articleBody:
Getting ready for trim work in a lower level requires verifying conditions before any cutting begins. A solid plan ensures trim stays flat, joints remain tight, and dampness doesn't ruin your investment.

- [ ] Check slab moisture levels — Make sure the concrete floor is dry and free of seepage so materials do not trap dampness.
- [ ] Acclimate trim boards on site — Keep wood or composite trim in the basement for 48 hours to match room humidity.
- [ ] Mark wall stud locations — Confirm solid wood framing behind the drywall for secure nail anchoring.
- [ ] Measure the entire room perimeter — Calculate linear footage and add 10 to 15 percent extra for miter cuts and waste.
- [ ] Inspect bottom wall plate clearances — Verify drywall stops slightly above the floor so baseboards seat cleanly.
- [ ] Select moisture-resistant materials — Choose PVC or composite trim if the basement experiences recurring dampness.
- [ ] Check corner squareness — Measure corners with an angle finder to adjust miter saw settings for imperfect drywall corners.
- [ ] Have paintable caulk and primer ready — Seal cut ends and back-prime real wood to prevent moisture absorption.

What to Prepare Before You Start:
Walk the room with a long level to spot dips in the floor or bowed studs in the framing. Knowing where the wall bows helps you determine whether to scribe boards or call an experienced carpenter.
